80	The trained $\dt$-embedding precedes CIVO in all five Walker Walk seeds (peak NVE: $4.72\times$, $4.62\times$, $4.12\times$, $1.62\times$, $1.53\times$), universally degrading performance to below 30\% of baseline (IQM $175.2$, mean $170.6$, $n{=}5$; \citealt{agarwal2021precipice}). Downstream trajectories diverge: two seeds undergo full collapse, one exhibits late-onset collapse still declining at 105K, and two self-correct (seeds 2 and 5). Combined with Cheetah Run (\S\ref{sec:f6}), CIVO onset is universal across all seven tested seeds ($n{=}7$, two environments) with 5/7 progressing toward collapse, 2/7 self-correcting (Appendix~\ref{sec:seed_divergence}).

86	\subsection{F3--F5: Factorial Ablation (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_factorial})}
87	\label{sec:f3f5_summary}
88	
89	Trained $\dt$-embedding and multi-rate data exposure are \emph{jointly sufficient in tested configurations} for CIVO. Neither factor alone precedes pathological overestimation: trained embedding without multi-rate exposure (008a, 3 seeds, peak NVE $0.83$--$0.93\times$) and multi-rate exposure without embedding (008f, 3 seeds, peak NVE $\leq 1.41\times$) both remain below $1.5\times$. Cross-environment replication on Cheetah Run confirms generalization. Freezing the embedding (\texttt{requires\_grad=False}) dramatically reduces severity (NVE $0.19$--$1.88\times$ vs.\ trained $1.53$--$4.72\times$; 2/4 seeds below threshold, 2/4 transient self-correcting spikes; Table~\ref{tab:three_way_emb}); removing the embedding (008f) also avoids CIVO. Partial gradient blocking (exp\_044) does not prevent onset (peak NVE $4.45\times$) but permits delayed self-correction (final eval 538, 59\% baseline; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_factorial}), confirming that \emph{any} gradient pathway updating $e_{\dt}$ suffices to induce CIVO. Degradation scales monotonically with $\dt$ ($-47\%$ at $\dt{=}2$, $-81\%$ at $\dt{=}4$; Figure~\ref{fig:dt_amplification}).

91	\paragraph{ManiSkill manipulation tasks.}
92	None of three ManiSkill environments exhibit $\dt$-embedding-dependent CIVO. StackCube-v1 value-ratio spikes are environment-specific: trained (049/052, NVE $5.05$/$4.67\times$) and frozen (051, $4.30\times$) match, all self-correcting by 82.5K. PegInsertionSide-v1 exhibits high-amplitude stochastic dynamics ($4$--$11\times$) whose trained/frozen ordering is seed-dependent: seed~0 trained peaks higher ($10.05\times$ vs.\ frozen $1.82\times$), but seed~1 reverses (frozen peak $11.32\times$ vs.\ trained peak $3.08\times$). PickCube-v1 frozen control (exp\_054, peak $8.81\times$ at 62.5K, self-correcting) confirms the same pattern. CIVO is locomotion-specific in DreamerV3; the frozen-embedding diagnostic correctly identifies these transients as non-CIVO.

101	\paragraph{F6: Trained embedding creates multiple vulnerability pathways.}
102	Exp\_008e\_v3 restricts imagination to $\dt{=}1$ while retaining the trained embedding. Two of four seeds collapse (50\%): Pathway~A (CIVO, $\nve = 4.02\times$) and preliminary Pathway~B (entropy \emph{increase}, $\nve = 3.78\times$; 2 seeds only, requires confirmation; Appendix~\ref{sec:pathways}). Pathway~B produces one of three non-CIVO false positives ($n{=}30$).
103	\paragraph{F7: Full-pathway gradient stopping shows mixed results.}
104	Full-SGS (exp\_018) detaches all non-KL gradients from $e_{\dt}$. Seed~1 shows partial mitigation (eval 448.3, NVE $1.66\times$); seed~2 collapses (0/2 elimination; Appendix~\ref{sec:sgs_gradient_analysis}). Cross-environment validation on Cheetah (010b, NVE $8.27$--$108.52\times$) confirms CIVO generalization; full-SGS yields 0/3 elimination. Removing the embedding eliminates CIVO on Cheetah (024b, NVE $< 0.2\times$).

400	\paragraph{Evidence B: trainability is necessary (exp\_015b).}
401	Exp\_015b uses a frozen random-projection embedding ($d{=}32$, \texttt{requires\_grad=False}, subsample ON, $H{=}8$), the same multi-rate data regime as exp\_008d, but with a non-trainable temporal signal. Despite full exposure to $\dt{>}1$ transitions, the NVE peaks at $1.45\times$ at 55K but does not sustain escalation: it retreats to $0.65\times$ by 65K and settles at $0.42\times$ by 105K (trajectory: $0.81 \rightarrow 1.26 \rightarrow 1.45 \rightarrow 0.65 \rightarrow 1.05 \rightarrow 0.47 \rightarrow 0.39 \rightarrow 0.42$). The transient peak approaches but does not exceed the $1.5\times$ CIVO threshold, and critically, the ratio self-corrects rather than exhibiting the monotonic escalation seen in trained-embedding runs. Final evaluation reaches only 204.2 at 105K, low but through a qualitatively different failure mode than CIVO. Actor loss approaches zero (gradient starvation; see \S\ref{sec:pathways}), the frozen embedding provides no useful gradient signal for temporal adaptation.
402	
403	The contrast with exp\_008d is stark: under identical data conditions (subsample ON, $H{=}8$), the trained embedding drives NVE to $4.12\times$ with sustained monotonic escalation ($1.78 \rightarrow 1.71 \rightarrow 2.09 \rightarrow 4.12$) and precedes full collapse (eval 82.8), while the frozen embedding peaks transiently at $1.45\times$ before self-correcting to $0.42\times$, a qualitative difference between sustained and transient overestimation. This demonstrates that a $\dt$-embedding must be able to \emph{co-adapt} with RSSM dynamics to produce the systematic reward-prediction bias that drives CIVO; a static random projection, regardless of its exposure to multi-rate data, cannot create this bias.
404	
405	Together, these two controls establish that in all tested configurations, CIVO occurs only with the \emph{joint} presence of (i)~a trainable embedding that can co-adapt with RSSM dynamics, and (ii)~multi-rate training data that drives this co-adaptation toward biased temporal predictions. Neither factor alone is sufficient.
406	
407	Cross-environment validation on Cheetah Run replicates the empirical pattern: trained $e_{\dt}$ precedes CIVO in both tested seeds (exp\_010b, 2 seeds, NVE $8.27$--$108.52\times$, collapse to 51.7/0.83) while removing the embedding eliminates it (exp\_024b, 2 seeds, NVE $<0.2\times$, eval 96.5/77.3). Freezing the embedding on Cheetah (exp\_046, NVE${=}1.35\times$ vs.\ trained $70.64\times$, a $52\times$ reduction) further confirms that embedding trainability, not architecture, drives CIVO. All seven CIVO-positive seeds cross the $\nve > 1.5\times$ threshold (Table~\ref{tab:post_civo}), yet the downstream damage is stochastic.\footnote{Exp\_009e was excluded from multi-seed analyses due to a seed configuration error (default seed=0, identical to exp\_008d).}  Full collapse is the majority outcome (5/7 seeds), with two self-correction cases (Walker seeds 2 and 5). Cheetah seeds exhibit more extreme overestimation (peak NVE $8.27$--$108.52\times$ vs.\ Walker's $1.53$--$4.62\times$), consistent with the Cheetah reward scale amplifying the fidelity gap.  We hypothesize that the divergence relates to the critic's representational capacity at the time of CIVO onset.  \citet{lyle2022capacity} demonstrate that deep RL networks suffer progressive capacity loss, in which early-learned features become increasingly difficult to overwrite.  If the critic's capacity is already partially consumed when CIVO injects overestimation, the network cannot recalibrate (seed~0); if sufficient capacity remains, the critic can absorb transient overestimation and recover (seed~2).
